title: Fit a U-joint cross longer than its yoke's ear gap: push one journal through, swing it level, slide it back to centre
instruction: Install the orange cross in the blue yoke: push one of its two flat journals through one ear's hole, swing the cross level so the other flat journal lines up with the other ear's hole, then slide it back until both journals are in their holes by the same depth.
context: Spicer Driveshafts Service Manual DSSM3264 (September 2007), Reassembly - Snap Ring Design, page 17, steps 2 and 3: "Position the journal cross in the yoke cross holes" and "Move one end of the journal cross to cause a trunnion to project through the cross hole beyond the outer machined face of the yoke ear." https://www.truckid.com/images/spicer/pdf/driveshafts-service-manual.pdf Done by: driveline and heavy-truck service technicians. The task ends at step 2, the cross sitting in both holes; until it does, no bearing cup can go on.
setup: Positions are from the midpoint between the arm bases, x out from the robot, y to its left. A fixed blue steel Spicer 1310 size tube yoke lies with its tube (76 mm across, 74 mm long) pointing away from the robot, on a grey steel stand (60 x 64 x 22 mm). Its two ears stand upright, 59.8 mm apart at their inner faces (estimated) and 81.8 mm over their outer faces, each 11 mm thick and round about its hole (22 mm radius), joined 30 mm behind the holes by the yoke's crotch. Each ear has a 27.0 mm cross hole (the bearing cap bore, caps removed); the holes share one axis across the table, at x 38 cm, y -16 cm, 61 mm above the table. A loose steel universal-joint cross with an orange hub (200 g) stands on one journal in a black plastic holder (four 6 mm walls, 16 mm tall, a 16 x 19 mm opening) at x 27 cm, y -16 cm. It has a 26 mm square hub and four 15 mm journals, 73 mm tip to tip in each pair (estimated); the flat pair is turned 76 degrees counter-clockwise (seen from above) from the holes' axis.
scoring: Either pair of journals can be the one that goes in; the pair nearer the holes' axis is scored. A journal is in its hole when the cross's centre is between the ears' inner faces, the journal's tip is at least 1 mm past its ear's inner face, and the tip's centre is within 8 mm of the holes' axis (inside a hole it can be 6 mm off at most). Installed: both journals of the pair in their holes, each tip at least 3.5 mm past its ear's inner face (6.6 mm when centred, so within 3.1 mm of centred), and the pair within 5 degrees of the holes' axis. 1.0 when installed and still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 1 s, which ends the trial. Otherwise the last step scores 0.75 if installed, 0.5 if both journals are in their holes (off centre or turned), 0.25 if one is, else 0. A cross pushed deep into one ear with its other journal out scores 0.25; one on the ears' tops, outside the yoke or in the holder scores 0. The scorer does not see the grippers, so a cross held in place counts the same as one let go.
reset_notes: Lift the cross out of the yoke and stand it back in its holder with its flat pair turned as the setup says.
fidelity: The yoke is fixed, as if clamped in a vise, and the cross is one rigid steel body with smooth journals (no needle rollers, seals or grease fitting). Hole and outer-face sizes are the Spicer 1310 catalog's (1.062 in caps, 3.219 in over the caps). The journals' 73 mm span and diameter, the ear thickness (so the 59.8 mm gap), hub size and mass are our estimates. Every object has rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (2,400 steps); demo: 1.0 (success at 33.5 s)
